_README: LAWS2 parameters. JSON, not YAML, so the frame needs nothing outside the standard library.
THREE CLASSES, and the distinction is the point:
research  - changes the CLAIM. Must be in the registration. Every one carries a `grid` of
defensible alternatives, and the specification-curve arm runs the law across that
grid and reports the DISTRIBUTION of effects instead of one point.
precision - changes the error bars, not the claim. Set by budget; the value is reported.
guard     - an implementation floor. Never silently binding: when one excludes a repo or a
snapshot, the exclusion is counted and published.
LAWS 1 had all of these as bare module constants, so a research choice and a bootstrap count
looked alike in the code and neither appeared in the registration.

hub_years_apart.why: 'still a hub five years later' - five is arbitrary, and LAW-3 is already the most fragile law

hub_top_share.why: who counts as a hub; a narrow cut puts the test on a handful of nodes

hub_still_share.why: how far a hub may fall and still 'persist'. With 0.05 the observed and null both sit near 0.95

hub_ceiling_sd.why: declares a repo 'not evaluable (ceiling)'. It silently decides WHICH repos the law is tested on

tail_min_fraction.why: the floor under 'the tail'. Observed tails ran 8% to 100% of nodes between repos

tail_min_nodes.why: a 30-node tail is too easy; the registration says so and then fixes one value

tail_xmin_rule.why: KS-chosen x_min is per-repo, so 'the tail' is not the same object across repos. A fixed x_min is comparable but less favourable

attach_features.why: a modelling choice written as a constant. Dropping log_loc tests whether attachment is size in disguise

snapshot_granularity.why: LAW-2 counts 'new edges per step'; the step length sets how many edges are new

frame_min_commits.why: did 95% of all rejection work in LAWS 1 - this parameter, not the research question, defined the population

frame_min_files.why: sets when a repo's history is judged to have started

frame_quarter_coverage.why: how gappy a history may be and still count

frame_language_share.why: how monolingual a repo must be to represent its language

coverage_ladder.why: the instrument control. 44% removal already moved LAW-3 by 157% and LAW-2 by 10%

seed.why: one seed everywhere; changing it is a re-draw, not a knob

incycle_gate.note: removed libxml2 from LAW-6 in LAWS 1 at an in-cycle share of 0.001
